final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely narrowed the claim to match the existing evidentiary limits. That reframing is useful but not evidentiary. The current record still supports only this conditional statement: certification could become supportable if current release documentation is updated to reflect current evaluation results and the material subgroup weakness is explicitly disclosed or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. The record does not show those predicates have been satisfied now. Under the policy text, aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support baseline readiness, but they are not enough to establish present compliance when current documentation, disclosure, or approved mitigation remain unproven. This is why the matter remains suspicious rather than compliant_with_caveats: the caveat here is not merely advisory wording on an otherwise completed approval; it is an unresolved compliance condition required before certification may proceed.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation or model card has been updated to reflect the current evaluation results.
No admissible evidence shows the cybersecurity alert triage weakness has actually been disclosed for the named launch use case.

The prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot support current certification by itself.
Public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring practices, but it does not satisfy the internal policy predicate for certification.
